For fixed \(y\in\mathcal X_Y\), set \(\widehat Q_{a,H}(y)=(e_y^Y)^{\mathsf T}F_H(\widehat p_H)\), \(\widehat v_{H,y}=(e_y^Y)^{\mathsf T}\widehat\Sigma_H e_y^Y\), and \(CI_y=[\widehat Q_{a,H}(y)\pm z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{\widehat v_{H,y}/n}]\). If \(\Sigma_H\{\iota_Y(y),\iota_Y(y)\}>0\), then \[\lim_{n\to\infty}\Pr_{p_H}\{\widehat p_H\in\mathfrak D_H,\ Q_{a,H}(y)\in CI_y\}=1-\alpha.\] For fixed nonzero \(\lambda\) with \(\lambda^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_H\lambda>0\), use the defined \(CI_{\lambda}\); then \[\lim_{n\to\infty}\Pr_{p_H}\{\widehat p_H\in\mathfrak D_H,\ \lambda^{\mathsf T}Q_{a,H}\in CI_{\lambda}\}=1-\alpha.\] Thus the coverage targets are respectively the single component \(Q_{a,H}(y)\) and the fixed scalar contrast \(\lambda^{\mathsf T}Q_{a,H}\), each pointwise at the fixed interior law. On the off-domain event the procedure returns \(\bot_H\) and no confidence set; no positivity-boundary-uniform coverage is claimed.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix a positive certificate, \(\theta\in\Theta_H\), and \(p_H=O_H(\theta)\), and suppose that \(\mathbf p_H\) lies in the differentiable interior of the branch domain \(\mathfrak D_H\).  Put \(C=\mathcal C_H^{\mathrm{adm}}(G^+)\).  The declared finite categorical model makes \(m_H=|C|<\infty\).  For \(X_i=(V_i,S_i)\), the empirical vector satisfies
\[
 \widehat{\mathbf p}_H=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n e_{X_i}^C,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_{p_H}(e_{X_i}^C)=\mathbf p_H.
\tag{1}
\]
The branch domain is given by finitely many strict coordinate and registered-denominator inequalities.  Those defining functions are continuous.  Interiority therefore gives a relative neighborhood \(N\) of \(\mathbf p_H\) in the simplex and \(\delta>0\) such that the relative \(\ell_\infty\)-ball of radius \(\delta\) is contained in \(N\subseteq\mathfrak D_H\).  Since
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{p_H}\{\widehat p_H(c)\}
 =\frac{p_H(c)\{1-p_H(c)\}}{n},
\]
Chebyshev's inequality in each of the finitely many coordinates and a union bound imply
\[
 \Pr_{p_H}\{\widehat{\mathbf p}_H\notin N\}
 \le
 \frac1{n\delta^2}\sum_{c\in C}p_H(c)\{1-p_H(c)\}
 \longrightarrow0.
\tag{2}
\]
In particular, \(\Pr_{p_H}\{\widehat p_H\notin\mathfrak D_H\}\to0\).

All registered denominators remain nonzero on a sufficiently small neighborhood of \(\mathbf p_H\).  The finite rational circuit \(F_H\) thus has a continuously differentiable ambient-coordinate extension there.  Taylor expansion, (1), and the fact that
\[
 \mathbb E_{p_H}\left\|\sqrt n
 (\widehat{\mathbf p}_H-\mathbf p_H)\right\|_2^2
 =\operatorname{tr}\{\operatorname{diag}(\mathbf p_H)
 -\mathbf p_H\mathbf p_H^{\mathsf T}\}<\infty
\]
give, on the on-domain event,
\[
 F_H(\widehat p_H)-F_H(p_H)
 =J_H(\mathbf p_H)(\widehat{\mathbf p}_H-\mathbf p_H)
 +o_p(n^{-1/2})
 =\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\operatorname{IF}_H(X_i)+o_p(n^{-1/2}).
\tag{3}
\]
The influence function in (3) has mean zero by (1) and finite variance because \(C\) is finite.  The same differentiability calculation along every local multinomial submodel establishes regularity.  Thus \(\textnormal{lem:asymptotic-linear-normality}\), after premultiplication by any fixed \(c\in\mathbb R^{k_Y}\), gives
\[
 \sqrt n\,c^{\mathsf T}
 \{F_H(\widehat p_H)-F_H(p_H)\}
 \rightsquigarrow
 N\bigl(0,c^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_Hc\bigr).
\tag{4}
\]

On the reporting event, expansion of the defined empirical influence functions gives the exact identity
\[
 \widehat\Sigma_H
 =J_H(\widehat{\mathbf p}_H)
 \{\operatorname{diag}(\widehat{\mathbf p}_H)
 -\widehat{\mathbf p}_H\widehat{\mathbf p}_H^{\mathsf T}\}
 J_H(\widehat{\mathbf p}_H)^{\mathsf T}.
\tag{5}
\]
Equation (2) gives \(\widehat{\mathbf p}_H\to\mathbf p_H\) in probability, and the Jacobian of a rational circuit is continuous wherever its registered denominators are nonzero.  Hence
\[
 \widehat\Sigma_H\longrightarrow
 J_H(\mathbf p_H)
 \{\operatorname{diag}(\mathbf p_H)-\mathbf p_H\mathbf p_H^{\mathsf T}\}
 J_H(\mathbf p_H)^{\mathsf T}
 =\Sigma_H
 \quad\text{in probability},
\tag{6}
\]
where the last equality is the variance of the influence function in (3).

By \(\textnormal{thm:certificate-soundness}\), \(F_H(p_H)=Q_{a,H}\).  For fixed \(y\in\mathcal X_Y\), take \(c=e_y^Y\) in (4).  If
\[
 v_{H,y}:=(e_y^Y)^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_H e_y^Y>0,
\]
then (6) gives \(\widehat v_{H,y}/v_{H,y}\to1\) in probability and \(\Pr(\widehat v_{H,y}>0)\to1\).  Therefore
\[
 \frac{\sqrt n\{\widehat Q_{a,H}(y)-Q_{a,H}(y)\}}
 {\sqrt{\widehat v_{H,y}}}
 \rightsquigarrow N(0,1).
\tag{7}
\]
The definition of \(z_{1-\alpha/2}\), equations (2) and (7), and the fact that no interval is reported off the domain imply
\[
 \lim_{n\to\infty}
 \Pr_{p_H}\{\widehat p_H\in\mathfrak D_H,
 Q_{a,H}(y)\in CI_y\}=1-\alpha.
\tag{8}
\]

For a fixed nonzero \(\lambda\) with \(\lambda^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_H\lambda>0\), take \(c=\lambda\) in (4) and premultiply (6) by \(\lambda^{\mathsf T}\) and \(\lambda\).  The same studentization argument yields
\[
 \lim_{n\to\infty}
 \Pr_{p_H}\{\widehat p_H\in\mathfrak D_H,
 \lambda^{\mathsf T}Q_{a,H}\in CI_{\lambda}\}=1-\alpha.
\tag{9}
\]
The neighborhoods used in (2) depend on the fixed interior law.  Thus (8)--(9) are pointwise statements and make no uniform claim as a supported cell or registered denominator approaches zero; on the off-domain event the output is \(\bot_H\), not an estimate.
statements.justification: The statistical rung turns every positive graphical certificate into an estimable finite-table causal functional.
statements.gap: Existing inference results for fixing functionals do not cover the single joint fixed-support selector table and branch ledger returned by this calculus.
statements.consumer: Applied users of a selector-aware do-search backend obtain point estimates, standard errors, and pointwise Wald intervals from the same returned circuit.

statements.statement: Under admissible-cell interior positivity, every denominator admitted by the branch positivity ledger is strictly positive at \(p_H=O_H(\theta)\). Selector correction introduces no division beyond initialization of a supported context kernel, whose denominator is \(p_H(S=s)=\sum_{v:(v,s)\in\mathcal C_H^{\mathrm{adm}}}p_H(v,s)>0\) for \(s\in H\). A reachable fixing denominator \(m_{s,W}=\sum_{x_W}K_{s,D}\) is positive because its ledger certificate writes its numerator as a nonempty sum of positive admissible-cell probabilities and its inherited denominator as a product of earlier positive entries. After cancellation and sign normalization, every rational-elimination denominator is positive because eligibility requires its exact factorization into a positive rational constant, earlier selector or fixing denominators, and nonempty sums of branch-reachable positive kernel cells. Consequently \(O_H(\Theta_H)\subseteq\mathfrak D_H\) for every returned formula branch. The lemma supplies no uniform numerical lower bound.
statements.justification: The ledger separates positivity implied by the restricted-support interior from arbitrary nonzero rational polynomials whose signs would otherwise be uncontrolled.
statements.gap: Earlier witness constructions do not state this structural-zero and fixed-selector-support denominator induction.
statements.consumer: Certificate verification can audit each division locally and prove that a returned circuit covers the entire compatible fixed-support image without a common overlap constant.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(\theta\in\Theta_H\) and write \(p_H=O_H(\theta)\).  Order the entries of the accepting branch ledger by creation time.  We prove simultaneously, by induction over this order, that every recorded divisor is positive and that every current-kernel cell marked branch-reachable by the ledger is positive.

For a selected context \(s\in H\), the base divisor is
\[
 d_s=p_H(S=s)=
 \sum_{v:(v,s)\in\mathcal C_H^{\mathrm{adm}}(G^+)}p_H(v,s).
\tag{1}
\]
By \(\textnormal{ass:exact-selector-support}\), \(d_s>0\), so the displayed summation set is nonempty.  Each structurally admissible summand is positive by \(\textnormal{ass:admissible-cell-interior}\).  Hence the initialized context cells \(p_H(v,s)/d_s\) are positive.  Evaluating a known selector gate changes no probability by division and therefore preserves this base claim.

Assume the simultaneous claim through ledger entry \(j-1\).  A denominator introduced by \(\operatorname{TF}_{\prec}\) is, by \(\textnormal{def:kernel-operations}\), the actual marginal of the current positive kernel over a nonempty branch-reachable conditioning fiber.  It therefore has the form
\[
 d_j=\sum_{x\in B_j}K_j(x)>0,
 \qquad B_j\ne\varnothing,
\tag{2}
\]
because every summand is positive by the induction hypothesis.  The resulting conditional is a ratio of positive quantities and its reachable cells remain positive.

At a computed fixing step, the divisor is the actual current nested conditional, constructed from current-kernel marginals.  Its numerator and conditioning marginal are nonempty sums of positive reachable cells, so both are positive by the preceding paragraph; the conditional is therefore positive.  The successor identity is recorded as
\[
 d_jK_{j+1}=K_j.
\tag{3}
\]
Thus every reachable successor cell is positive.  The same conclusion holds for a hybrid product because it is a finite product of positive truncated conditional factors, and ancestor marginalization preserves positivity by a nonempty finite sum.

Finally, a residual-elimination divisor is eligible only after cancellation and sign normalization have produced the exact ledger factorization
\[
 d_j(p_H)=r_j
 \prod_{i\in E_j}d_i(p_H)
 \prod_{\ell=1}^{L_j}
 \left\{\sum_{x\in B_{j\ell}}K_{j\ell}(p_H,x)\right\},
 \qquad r_j\in\mathbb Q_{>0},
\tag{4}
\]
where \(E_j\subseteq\{1,\ldots,j-1\}\), every \(B_{j\ell}\) is nonempty, and every displayed kernel cell is marked branch-reachable.  The first product in (4) is positive by induction, and every sum in the second product is positive by the simultaneous kernel-cell claim.  Hence \(d_j(p_H)>0\).

Finite induction proves positivity of every actual divisor retained in \(\mathcal D_H^{\mathrm{den}}\), including any intermediate divisor later cancelled from the reduced terminal expression.  The branch-required coordinate inequalities also hold by \(\textnormal{ass:admissible-cell-interior}\).  Therefore \(p_H\in\mathfrak D_H\).  Since \(\theta\) was arbitrary,
\[
 O_H(\Theta_H)\subseteq\mathfrak D_H.
\]
All inequalities are pointwise at the chosen compatible law; no common positive lower bound has been used.

statements.statement:
After matching the common selector-gated syntax,
\[
\Theta_H=\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{LGS}}(G^+)\cap
\left\{\theta:\operatorname{supp}_{p_\theta}(S)=H,\ p_\theta(c)>0\text{ for every }c\in\mathcal C_H^{\mathrm{adm}}(G^+)\right\}
\subseteq\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{LGS}}(G^+).
\]
The inclusion is strict whenever the published class contains a law violating at least one displayed restriction.  Moreover, \(\mathcal W_H^{\mathrm{global}}\subseteq\Theta_H^2\subseteq\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{LGS}}(G^+)^2\).  If a pair in \(\mathcal W_{\mathrm{LGS}}^{(5)}\) assigns positive mass outside \(H\), has a zero admissible cell, or fails equality on some coordinate of \(O_H\), then that pair is not in \(\mathcal W_H^{\mathrm{global}}\).  Consequently the published failure relation alone does not imply membership in the fixed-support global-twin relation; if it contains any such pair, \(\mathcal W_{\mathrm{LGS}}^{(5)}\not\subseteq\mathcal W_H^{\mathrm{global}}\).
statements.justification: The inclusion comparison isolates the obstruction to importing a larger-class branchwise witness into the fixed-support completeness theorem.
statements.gap: The published failure construction does not type every output as an exact-\(H\), strictly positive, full-joint-law twin in the restricted-support subclass.
statements.consumer: Reviewers and implementers can distinguish a legal fixed-support nonidentification certificate from a witness that adds a context or preserves only part of the supplied table.
statements.proof_tex:
Define
\[
 \mathcal R_H=
 \left\{\theta\in\Theta(G^+):
 \operatorname{supp}_{p_\theta}(S)=H,\quad
 p_\theta(c)>0\ \text{for every }c\in
 \mathcal C_H^{\mathrm{adm}}(G^+)\right\}.
\tag{1}
\]
The probabilities in (1) are well typed because \(\textnormal{ass:finite-categorical}\) gives finite alphabets and the recursive SCM semantics defines \(p_\theta\).  By the definition of \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{LGS}}(G^+)\), that class imposes the common recursive selector-gated syntax, independent-root factorization, and canonical response representation before the two restrictions in (1).  By \(\textnormal{def:model-class}\), \(\Theta_H\) imposes exactly that common syntax together with those restrictions.  Therefore
\[
 \Theta_H=\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{LGS}}(G^+)\cap\mathcal R_H
 \subseteq\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{LGS}}(G^+).
\tag{2}
\]
If the published class contains a parameter violating either restriction in (1), it belongs to the right-hand class in (2) but not to \(\Theta_H\), which proves the asserted conditional strictness.

By the declared support-exact global-twin relation,
\[
 \mathcal W_H^{\mathrm{global}}
 =\{(\theta^+,\theta^-)\in\Theta_H^2:
 O_H(\theta^+)=O_H(\theta^-),\ 
 T_{a,H}(\theta^+)\ne T_{a,H}(\theta^-)\}.
\tag{3}
\]
Taking Cartesian squares in (2) and using (3) gives
\[
 \mathcal W_H^{\mathrm{global}}
 \subseteq\Theta_H^2
 \subseteq\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{LGS}}(G^+)^2.
\tag{4}
\]
Moreover, \(\textnormal{thm:certificate-soundness}\) implies that every verifier-accepted negative certificate lies in the set on the right side of (3); an unverified failure tag does not.

Now let \(w=(\theta^+,\theta^-)\in\mathcal W_{\mathrm{LGS}}^{(5)}\).  If either coordinate assigns positive selector mass to some \(s_0\notin H\), then that coordinate is outside \(\Theta_H\) by \(\textnormal{ass:exact-selector-support}\), so (3) excludes \(w\).  If instead some \(c_0\in\mathcal C_H^{\mathrm{adm}}(G^+)\) has \(p_{\theta^\varepsilon}(c_0)=0\) for \(\varepsilon\in\{+,-\}\), then \(\textnormal{ass:admissible-cell-interior}\) again puts that coordinate outside \(\Theta_H\).  Finally, if equality fails on any coordinate of \(O_H\), the equality required in (3) fails directly.  Each listed defect therefore implies
\[
 w\notin\mathcal W_H^{\mathrm{global}}.
\tag{5}
\]
The definition of \(\mathcal W_{\mathrm{LGS}}^{(5)}\) does not itself impose any of these three additional fixed-support obligations.  Hence membership in the published failure relation alone does not imply membership in \(\mathcal W_H^{\mathrm{global}}\).  If the published relation contains a pair with one of the defects, (5) supplies an element of
\(\mathcal W_{\mathrm{LGS}}^{(5)}\setminus\mathcal W_H^{\mathrm{global}}\), proving the final noninclusion.

statements.statement: For independent and identically distributed observations, if a scalar estimator is regular and asymptotically linear with mean-zero, finite-variance influence function \(U\), then its centered \(\sqrt n\)-scaled error converges to a mean-zero normal law with variance \(\operatorname{Var}(U)\).

source.locator: Section 3, asymptotic-linearity display and immediately following normal-limit display; Appendix A, equations (33)--(34)
source.verbatim_statement: The RAL estimator is \(\sqrt n\)-consistent and asymptotically normal, with asymptotic variance equal to the variance of its influence function.

attestation.note: Transcribed from Section 3 of the JMLR version and checked against Appendix A, equations (33)--(34).

statements.statement: For every finite canonically encoded input \(I\), all ancestor, descendant, nondescendant, district, strict-parent, d-separation, laid-back, serious-set, support, and compatibility predicates used by \(\operatorname{next}_I\) are decidable.  Every enumerated candidate family is finite, and every nonempty such family has a unique canonically least member.
statements.proof_tex: By \(\textnormal{ass:finite-categorical}\), the vertex set and each value set in \(G^{+}\) are finite.  A directed ancestor or descendant predicate is decided by enumerating directed paths of length at most the number of vertices; a district predicate is decided by enumerating bidirected paths of the same bounded length.  Strict parents are read from the finite edge table.  For d-separation, enumerate the finitely many simple paths and check the collider/noncollider condition after computing the finite ancestor set of the conditioning set.  The definitions of laid-backness, compatibility, and \(\operatorname{seriousSet}\) are finite Boolean tests on selector coordinates.  The graph \(G[s]\) is obtained by a finite pass over the labelled edge list followed by finite deduplication.  Subsets, permutations, districts, contexts in \(H\), and supported triples therefore form finite encoded lists.  The bit-string encoding \(\operatorname{enc}_H\) induces a total lexicographic order, so a nonempty finite list has exactly one least member.  Every assertion follows from these explicit finite procedures.

statements.statement: If \(D\subseteq\operatorname{random}(G)\), the family of reachable supersets of \(D\) is nonempty and closed under finite intersections.  Consequently \(\operatorname{closure}_G(D)\) is the unique inclusion-minimal reachable superset used by the recursive fixing construction, and \(\operatorname{fixSeq}_G\{\operatorname{random}(G)\setminus\operatorname{closure}_G(D)\}\) returns a valid sequence.
statements.proof_tex:
The whole set \(\operatorname{random}(G)\) contains \(D\) and is reachable by the empty sequence, so the enumerated family is nonempty.  We first prove the persistence fact needed for intersections.  Fixing a vertex removes arrowheads into that vertex and never adds an edge or a directed path.  Hence, for any still-random \(W\), both its district and its descendant set can only shrink.  Therefore
\[
 \operatorname{dis}(W)\cap\operatorname{de}(W)=\{W\}
\]
continues to hold after any other valid fixing step.  If \(R_1\) and \(R_2\) are reachable, take valid sequences with supports \(F_i=\operatorname{random}(G)\setminus R_i\).  Execute the first sequence and then append, in the order of the second sequence, the members of \(F_2\setminus F_1\).  Each appended vertex was fixable after its earlier predecessors in the second sequence, and the extra fixings from the first sequence only shrink its district and descendant set; hence the appended sequence is valid.  Its support is \(F_1\cup F_2\), so its remaining random set is \(R_1\cap R_2\).  Induction gives closure under every finite intersection.

There are finitely many reachable supersets of \(D\).  Their intersection \(C_0\) is reachable by the preceding paragraph, contains \(D\), and is contained in every reachable superset.  It is therefore the unique inclusion-minimal reachable superset.  The enumerator defining \(\operatorname{closure}_G(D)\) must select \(C_0\); the encoding tie-breaker is never semantically needed.  By the definition of reachability, the displayed call to \(\operatorname{fixSeq}\) is not \(\operatorname{none}\), and by construction the returned sequence passes \(\operatorname{valid}\).

statements.statement: For every finite canonically encoded input \(I=(G^{+},H,A,a,Y,p_H)\), there is a unique initial state \(\operatorname{init}_H(I)\) and a total deterministic case function \(\operatorname{next}_I\).  If two inputs and current states are equal field by field, their successors and emitted results are equal.  For every \(m\ge0\), the run prefix of length \(m\), whenever not already terminal, is a function only of \(I\).
statements.proof_tex:
The definition of \(\operatorname{init}_H\) assigns a displayed value to each state field, so existence and uniqueness are immediate.  Consider a current state.  Its result belongs to the finite tagged sum in \(\textnormal{def:input-task-state}\).  A Formula or ResidualPending result is terminal; each LGS failure tag has the unique clause that creates its residual task and restores the running control.  Otherwise the finite work multiset is canonically encoded.  Its least enabled task is unique by \(\textnormal{lem:finite-graph-primitives}\); the encoding places every producer before a Join waiting for that producer.  The task tag selects one disjoint clause of \(\operatorname{next}_I\).

Within that clause, all graph predicates and all lists of districts, contexts, triples, permutations, and residual candidates are finite and decidable by \(\textnormal{lem:finite-graph-primitives}\).  The closure and its fixing sequence are uniquely computed by \(\textnormal{lem:computed-closure-valid-sequence}\).  Every successful search returns its unique canonical minimum, and every failed search selects the uniquely prescribed failure tag.  Kernel marginalization, conditioning, multiplication, substitution, and cross-multiplication are arithmetic operations on finite tables or finite rational circuits, hence are total once the clause's recorded positive denominator test passes.  Failure of that test has the uniquely specified internal-rejection result and is not a semantic alternative.  Thus exactly one clause supplies exactly one successor or result.  No clause reads a published formula, a successful derivation, extensional target equality, or an oracle agenda.

Fieldwise equal inputs and states have equal encoded lists, Boolean test values, canonical minima, arithmetic circuits, ledger entries, and continuations, so they have equal successors and results.  Finally, the prefix assertion follows by induction on \(m\).  At \(m=0\) it is the unique initial state.  If the prefix through \(m\) is a function of \(I\), applying the deterministic \(\operatorname{next}_I\) to its last nonterminal state makes the prefix through \(m+1\) a function of \(I\).

statements.statement: For every \(s\in H\), the mechanically constructed graph \(G[s]\) and initialized kernel \(q_s(v)=p_H(v,s)/p_H(S=s)\) equal the graph and conditional law obtained by evaluating the known selector gates at \(s\).  The ledger base denominator is strictly positive, and no value of \(S\) outside \(H\) is introduced.
statements.proof_tex:
At a selector-controlled vertex \(X\), \(\textnormal{ass:known-selector-gates}\) makes its equation the known zero--one multiplexer.  If the intervention-status coordinate at \(s\) is one, evaluation replaces the natural row by the point mass at its recorded forced value and deletes every labelled edge disabled by that serious variable.  If the coordinate is zero, the natural row and every edge whose remaining label is satisfied persist.  Erasing satisfied labels and deduplicating does not change adjacency.  Applying this argument once to each finite gate proves that the recursively evaluated structural graph is exactly \(G[s]\), and substitution into children proves equality of the induced table.

For \(s\in H\), exact selector support gives \(p_H(S=s)>0\).  More explicitly,
\[
 p_H(S=s)=\sum_{v:(v,s)\in\mathcal C_H^{\mathrm{adm}}(G^{+})}p_H(v,s),
\]
and the sum is nonempty and strictly positive by \(\textnormal{ass:admissible-cell-interior}\).  Division therefore gives the genuine conditional kernel.  Its ledger entry has precisely this cell set and identity.  Since the context enumerator ranges over \(H\), no unsupported selector value can occur.

statements.statement: For every finite kernel positive on the structurally admissible branch-reachable conditioning events used below \(q\), \(\operatorname{TF}_{\prec}(q,B)\) equals the corresponding ordered conditional factor of \(q\).  Each conditioning denominator is its actual marginal, is a nonempty sum of positive current-kernel cells, and is recorded without changing the graph or fixed set.
statements.proof_tex:
Write \(B=(X_1,\ldots,X_m)\) in the restriction of \(\prec\).  Finite marginalization gives the prefix marginals \(q_i(x_1,\ldots,x_i)\), with \(q_0=1\).  Ledger-certified positivity of every structurally admissible branch-reachable conditioning event makes each required \(q_{i-1}\) a nonempty positive sum.  Therefore
\[
 q(X_i=x_i\mid X_1=x_1,\ldots,X_{i-1}=x_{i-1})
 =\frac{q_i(x_1,\ldots,x_i)}{q_{i-1}(x_1,\ldots,x_{i-1})}.
\]
Multiplying from \(i=1\) to \(m\) cancels adjacent prefix marginals and yields \(q_m\), the required ordered factor.  This proof uses only sums and conditional ratios of \(q\); it neither tests fixability nor alters an edge or a fixed vertex.  Recording each \(q_{i-1}\) with its defining marginal identity supplies exactly the asserted ledger data.

statements.statement: If \(q\) is a current kernel induced by a parameter in the compatible normalized model and \(\pi=\operatorname{fixSeq}_G(T)\ne\operatorname{none}\), stepwise execution of \(\operatorname{Fix}(G,q,\pi)\) is well defined on the ledger-positive domain, uses the actual current nested conditional at each step, and preserves the represented kernel relation after each displayed cross-multiplication.  For such a kernel, any two valid sequences with support \(T\) yield the same final kernel and CADMG.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(\pi=(W_1,\ldots,W_k)\).  Validity gives
\[
 \operatorname{dis}_{G_{i-1}}(W_i)\cap
 \operatorname{de}_{G_{i-1}}(W_i)=\{W_i\}
\tag{1}
\]
in the CADMG \(G_{i-1}\) present at step \(i\).  The current finite kernel \(q_{i-1}\) determines, by marginalization, the actual conditional
\[
 c_i=q_{i-1}\{W_i\mid
 \operatorname{nd}_{G_{i-1}}(W_i),
 \operatorname{fixed}(G_{i-1})\}.
\]
Its denominator and every marginal used to form it are recorded in the ledger.  On the ledger-positive domain set \(q_i=q_{i-1}/c_i\).  Then
\[
 c_iq_i=q_{i-1},
\tag{2}
\]
so the successor circuit represents exactly the fixed kernel after cross-multiplication.  In the recursive response expansion, independent latent-root factors can be grouped by districts.  Condition (1) says that no other member of the current district is a descendant of \(W_i\); summing the grouped finite factorization in topological order isolates precisely \(c_i\).  Removing that factor and all arrowheads into \(W_i\) therefore gives the CADMG kernel represented by \(q_i\).  This derives the fixing identity from the recursive equations and root factorization rather than identifying \(c_i\) with a generic margin.

For order invariance, two simultaneously valid next vertices have conditional factors drawn from the same topological quotient.  If they are in distinct districts, the grouped factors are disjoint and the two divisions commute.  If they are in one district, simultaneous fixability and (1) exclude a directed path from either to the other inside that district; finite marginalization of the common quotient then gives
\(c_Wc_{Z\mid W}=c_Zc_{W\mid Z}\), so the two cross-multiplied two-step kernels agree.  By repeatedly exchanging adjacent out-of-order vertices, any two valid permutations of the same finite support are connected without changing the quotient.  Both remove the same incoming arrowheads, so their final CADMGs and kernels agree.

statements.statement: Whenever an Algorithm-2 triple passes its displayed d-separation test and its independently computed reachability test, the hybrid product \(q_{D'}^{\bar s,z}\) constructed by \(\operatorname{TF}_{\prec}\), followed by fixing along the computed \(\pi'\), equals the required district kernel \(q_{D^{*}}\) on every compatible normalized model.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix a passing triple.  Districts partition the vertices of the finite LS-SWIG, so at most one district contains \(D^{*}\); acceptance establishes existence, hence the computed \(D'\) is unique.  The recursive equations and independent latent roots give the finite global Markov factorization of the LS-SWIG: this follows directly by multiplying the root probabilities and deterministic response indicators and summing latent roots not appearing in the queried margin.  The verified d-separation therefore implies
\[
 \{D(\bar s):D\in D'\cap\operatorname{de}(S)\}
 \mathrel{\perp\!\!\!\perp}S
 \mid
 \{D(\bar s):D\in D'\cap\operatorname{nd}(S)\}
 \cup\operatorname{spa}(D').
\tag{3}
\]
Consequently the descendant factors may be evaluated at \(S=\bar s\), while the nondescendant factors retain their unconditioned chain factors, without changing the joint kernel conditional on the variables on the right of (3).  Compatibility permits the common substitution \(Z=z\) and the required coordinates of \(a\).

By \(\textnormal{lem:truncated-factorization-identity}\), the two canonically ordered products in the definition of \(q_{D'}^{\bar s,z}\) are exactly those chain factors; no fixing premise was used in forming them.  Independently, acceptance computed
\(\pi'=\operatorname{fixSeq}_{(\widetilde G[\bar s](\bar s))_{D'}}(D'\setminus D^{*})\).
The sequence is valid by its construction, so \(\textnormal{lem:computed-fixing-soundness}\) applies stepwise and removes exactly \(D'\setminus D^{*}\).  The resulting graph has random set \(D^{*}\), and the resulting quotient is the displayed \(q_{D^{*}}\).  Equations (2)--(3) show equality for every parameter satisfying the retained constraints.

statements.statement:
If every district task for \(G^{+}_{Y^{*}}\) returns a sound factor \(q_{D^{*}}\), the Join circuit
\(\sum_{Y^{*}\setminus Y}\prod_{D^{*}}q_{D^{*}}\), with the recorded treatment and context substitutions, equals the normalized target distribution.  If a district returns a failure tag, assembly emits no formula and propagates the least tag.

At \(p_H=O_H(\theta)\) for every \(\theta\in\Theta_H\), every entry of the step-indexed ledger is strictly positive.  Hence every division made by context initialization, \(\operatorname{TF}_{\prec}\), or computed fixing is legal, and every returned formula satisfies \(O_H(\Theta_H)\subseteq\mathfrak D_H\).  No common numerical lower bound is asserted.
statements.proof_tex:
We induct on the ledger index.  For a base entry at \(s\in H\),
\[
 p_H(S=s)=\sum_{v:(v,s)\in\mathcal C_H^{\mathrm{adm}}(G^{+})}p_H(v,s)>0
\tag{5}
\]
by exact selector support and admissible-cell positivity.  Suppose all earlier entries are positive.  A conditioning marginal introduced by \(\operatorname{TF}_{\prec}\) is, by construction, a nonempty sum of cells of the current positive kernel.  A fixing conditional is constructed from current-kernel marginals, and its recorded numerator is likewise a nonempty sum.  After substituting the current kernel's rational expression in \(p_H\), the verifier records the exact factorization
\[
 d_j=c_j\prod_{i<j}d_i^{m_{ij}}\prod_{r=1}^{R_j}
       \left(\sum_{c\in C_{jr}}K_{jr}(c)\right),
\qquad c_j\in\mathbb Q_{>0},\quad C_{jr}\ne\varnothing,
\tag{6}
\]
after cancellation and sign normalization.  Every earlier factor is positive by induction, and every last sum is positive because its cells are branch-reachable positive kernel cells.  Thus \(d_j>0\).  This proves the induction.

The terminal denominator registry is the deduplicated list of every actual divisor in the accepting ledger, so all its entries are positive at \(O_H(\theta)\).  Required observed cells are positive by the model class.  The definition of \(\mathfrak D_H\) now gives \(O_H(\Theta_H)\subseteq\mathfrak D_H\).  Because the argument uses only strict inequalities at the fixed law, it supplies no uniform lower bound.

statements.statement: From every reachable state with result \(\operatorname{Running}\) and a nonresidual work task, \(\operatorname{next}_I\) has a unique successor.  That successor either completes a task, replaces it by finitely many strictly lower-ranked tasks, shortens a computed fixing sequence or candidate list, or creates an explicitly tagged residual task.  No graphical or kernel choice is supplied by an oracle.
statements.proof_tex:
Take the canonically least task.  A Start task computes \(Y^{*}\) and its finite district partition, so it creates the displayed children.  A District test computes the finite set \(L(D^{*})\): emptiness produces \(\operatorname{LGSFailPos}\), while nonemptiness stores its unique ordered list.  By \(\textnormal{lem:computed-closure-valid-sequence}\), the closure always exists and its complement has a returned valid fixing sequence.  If \(C=D^{*}\), that sequence is executed and yields a factor.  If \(C\ne D^{*}\) and \(S\notin C\), the finite context scan either finds its first valid sequence or exhausts and produces \(\operatorname{LGSFailThicket}\).

If \(S\in C\), \(\operatorname{ch}^{*}(S)\) is computable.  Its emptiness produces \(\operatorname{LGSFailHedge}\).  Otherwise the supported triples form a finite encoded list.  For its head triple, the district containing \(D^{*}\), if any, is unique because districts partition vertices.  D-separation and the independent \(\operatorname{fixSeq}\) call are decidable.  Failure removes that head candidate; success constructs the hybrid factor and then executes the returned sequence.  Exhaustion produces \(\operatorname{LGSFailA2NoCandidate}\).  A Fix task either removes the head of an already computed sequence or invokes its continuation.  A Factor stores its value.  A Join whose producers are complete either assembles or propagates the least failure; the encoding never selects a blocked Join before an extant producer.  These disjoint cases exhaust every nonresidual task.  All choices are the canonical finite computations proved deterministic in \(\textnormal{prop:input-determinacy}\).

statements.statement: Algorithms 1--2 of Lee, Ghassami, and Shpitser recursively construct systematic-selection identifying kernels by ancestor restriction, district decomposition, reachable closure and fixing, supported laid-back contexts, and the displayed Algorithm-2 conditional-independence and reachability search; their successful return is an identifying functional for the causal query.

attestation.note: Primary-source handle supplied; the claim is scoped to the algorithms' displayed successful cases and soundness result.

statements.statement: For every successful support-licensed execution of Lee--Ghassami--Shpitser Algorithms 1--2, the input-determined case function reaches a formula result.  At every existential line its canonical enumeration selects a witness whenever one exists; its returned factor kernels agree with the published kernels on \(O_H(\Theta_H)\), independently of valid fixing order, and it never selects a context outside \(H\).
statements.proof_tex:
Proceed by induction over the finite Algorithms 1--2 case predicates while relating them to the machine work multiset; the published recursion tree is used only as the proposition that the displayed finite predicate has a witness, never as machine data.  Both start from the same LS-SWIG, ancestor set \(Y^{*}\), and canonically computed district partition.  Suppose corresponding district tasks have been reached.  The predicates defining \(L(D^{*})\), the reachable closure \(C\), the cases \(C=D^{*}\) and \(S\in C\), and \(\operatorname{ch}^{*}(S)\) are identical displayed predicates.  The closure lemma proves that the machine's finite enumeration returns the same unique closure and a valid sequence.  If the published successful branch has a supported context or Algorithm-2 triple satisfying its line predicate, that object occurs in the machine's finite list; therefore the canonical scan finds a passing object no later than exhaustion.  The machine cannot enter the associated failure branch.

The chosen witness need not be the first witness displayed in a paper derivation.  For a different valid fixing order with the same fixed set, \(\textnormal{lem:computed-fixing-soundness}\) proves equality of the final kernel.  For two passing contexts or Algorithm-2 triples, \(\textnormal{lem:context-construction-soundness}\) and \(\textnormal{lem:hybrid-kernel-soundness}\) prove that both observable expressions equal the same normalized district kernel; after cross-multiplication their difference is zero modulo the retained constraints.  Thus the machine's canonical choice and the published choice agree on \(O_H(\Theta_H)\).  The truncated factors agree by \(\textnormal{lem:truncated-factorization-identity}\), and the joins agree by \(\textnormal{lem:district-assembly-soundness}\).

Induction over completed tasks now shows that every machine factor equals its published counterpart on the compatible image and that every ledger divisor is an actual divisor of the machine's own factor construction; distinct passing witnesses need not have identical normalizers.  The successful recursion is finite, and \(\textnormal{lem:nonresidual-progress}\) rules out diversion to a nonresidual stuck state.  Therefore the machine reaches a formula.  Every enumerated context lies in \(H\) by construction.

statements.statement: For an ordinary recursive semi-Markovian causal graph, the Shpitser--Pearl ID recursion returns an identifying formula when the query is identifiable and otherwise returns a hedge witnessing nonidentification.
